title: Count Nice Pairs in an Array
summary: Given an array of non-negative integers, count the number of index pairs (i, j) where 0 <= i < j < array length, and the sum of the number at i and the reverse of the number at j equals the sum of the number at j and the reverse of the number at i.
statement: Given an array of non-negative integers, count the number of index pairs (i, j) where 0 <= i < j < array length, and the sum of the number at i and the reverse of the number at j equals the sum of the number at j and the reverse of the number at i. Return the count modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: rev(x) reverses decimal digits and discards leading zeros in the result.
hints: Rearrange the equality so each side depends on only one array value.
Two values form a nice pair exactly when value-rev(value) is equal.
Count earlier occurrences of each transformed key while scanning.
The algebraic transformation is equivalent to the original equation, and adding prior frequency counts each ordered index pair once.
editorial: The algebraic transformation is equivalent to the original equation, and adding prior frequency counts each ordered index pair once.

tests.explanation: Pairs 42/97 and 11/1 share the required transformed value, so the answer is two.
Four index pairs satisfy the equality.
